title: Chicken Little
subtitle: A traditional folk tale • Also known as Henny-Penny • A funny bedtime tale about panicking — and checking for acorns.

cover.alt: Henny-penny, Cocky-locky, Ducky-daddles, Goosey-poosey, and Turkey-lurkey hurrying down the country path together.

blocks.html: One day Henny-penny was picking up corn in the rickyard under the big oak tree.

blocks.alt: Henny-penny the little brown hen pecks corn happily under the big oak tree.
blocks.caption: Henny-penny pecks corn in the sunny rickyard.

blocks.html: Whack! An acorn hit her upon the head.

🐔 Henny-penny
“Goodness gracious me! The sky's a-going to fall; I must go and tell the King.”

blocks.alt: An acorn bonks the startled hen on the head under the oak tree.
blocks.caption: Whack! An acorn hits her on the head!

blocks.html: So she went along, and she went along, and she went along...

🐔 Henny-penny
“The sky's a-falling! The sky's a-falling!”

blocks.alt: The panicked hen runs flapping down the country lane.
blocks.caption: She runs down the lane in a panic.

blocks.html: Till she met Cocky-locky.

🐓 Cocky-locky
“Where are you going, Henny-penny?” — “Oh! I'm going to tell the King the sky's a-falling.” — “May I come with you?” — “Certainly!”

blocks.alt: Henny-penny meets Cocky-locky the proud rooster on the lane.
blocks.caption: Cocky-locky joins the march.

blocks.html: They went along, and they went along, till they met Ducky-daddles.

🦆 Ducky-daddles
“Oh! we're going to tell the King the sky's a-falling.” — “May I come with you?” — “Certainly!”

blocks.alt: The hen and rooster meet Ducky-daddles the little yellow duck by the pond.
blocks.caption: Ducky-daddles waddles along too.

blocks.html: They went along, and they went along, till they met Goosey-poosey.

🪿 Goosey-poosey
“Oh! we're going to tell the King the sky's a-falling.” — “May I come with you?” — “Certainly!”

blocks.alt: The three birds meet Goosey-poosey the elegant white goose in the meadow.
blocks.caption: Goosey-poosey bends her long neck to listen.

blocks.html: They went along, and they went along, till they met Turkey-lurkey.

🦃 Turkey-lurkey
“May I come with you?” — “Oh, certainly!”

blocks.alt: All five birds hurry together down the country path.
blocks.caption: The whole flock hurries along together.

blocks.html: They went along, and they went along, till they met Foxy-woxy at the edge of the dark wood.

🦊 Foxy-woxy
“Oh! but this is not the way to the King. I know the proper way; shall I show it you?” — “Oh, certainly, Foxy-woxy!”

blocks.alt: The sly fox smiles cunningly at the five worried birds.
blocks.caption: Foxy-woxy offers to show the way.

blocks.html: So they went along, and they went along, till they came to a narrow and dark hole. This was the door of Foxy-woxy's burrow.

🦊 Foxy-woxy
“This is the short cut to the King's palace. Follow me!”

blocks.alt: The fox points at the narrow dark burrow hole while the birds peer nervously.
blocks.caption: A narrow, dark hole — the fox's burrow.

blocks.html: So Foxy-woxy slipped into the dark burrow, and turned round to wait. Now Turkey-lurkey was the first to go through the dark hole into the burrow.

blocks.alt: Inside the dark burrow, the fox waits with glinting eyes as Turkey-lurkey steps in.
blocks.caption: Turkey-lurkey is the first to step inside.

blocks.html: He hadn't got far when — “Hrumph!” Foxy-woxy snapped off Turkey-lurkey's head. Then Goosey-poosey went in, and — “Hrumph!” Then Ducky-daddles waddled down, and — “Hrumph!”

blocks.alt: The worried birds wait outside the dark hole as the fox's tail disappears inside.
blocks.caption: One by one, the friends go into the dark.

blocks.html: Then Cocky-locky strutted down into the burrow. But Cocky-locky will always crow whether you want him to do so or not...

🐓 Cocky-locky
“Cock-a-doodle-doo!”

blocks.alt: Cocky-locky throws his head back and crows with all his might in the dark.
blocks.caption: Cocky-locky crows with all his might!

blocks.html: Now when Henny-penny, who had just got into the dark burrow, heard Cocky-locky crow...

🐔 Henny-penny
“My goodness! It must be dawn. Time for me to lay my egg.”

blocks.alt: Henny-penny turns and bustles out of the dark hole into bright daylight.
blocks.caption: Henny-penny turns and bustles off to her nest.

blocks.html: So she escaped — but she never told the King the sky was falling!

blocks.alt: Henny-penny sits safely in her cozy straw nest at dawn.
blocks.caption: Safe in her nest — but the King never heard!

blocks.html: After all, the sky was never falling at all. It was only ever an acorn. The end.

blocks.alt: Henny-penny gazes thoughtfully at a single acorn under the oak tree.
blocks.caption: It was only ever an acorn. The end.

discussionHtml:
💭 Bedtime Chat

What should Henny-penny have done before running to tell the King?

🐔 Check First Henny-penny never looked up to see what hit her! When something surprises you, take a breath and check what really happened before you panic.
🦊 Beware of Flattery Foxy-woxy tricked the birds by pretending to help. Be careful of strangers offering shortcuts — and always tell a grown-up where you are going.
